definitions.gloss: karuta; Japanese card game; playing cards (traditional)
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese card game in which players compete to quickly grab cards that match a clue read aloud. Also refers to the cards themselves.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧かるた⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To play karuta at New Year's.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧かるた{取|と}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しんでいる→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧。
examples.english: The children are enjoying a game of karuta.

notes:
From Portuguese 'carta' (card). A traditional Japanese card game with several varieties.

TYPES OF KARUTA:
- いろはかるた: proverb-based karuta for children
- ⟦{百人一首|ひゃくにんいっしゅ}→百人一首：22329_hyakuninisshu⟧: classical poetry karuta (100 famous poems)
- ⟦{競技|きょうぎ}→競技：02606_kyougi⟧かるた: competitive karuta — a serious sport with ranked players

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- かるた⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to play karuta
- かるた{取|と}り: playing karuta (the act of grabbing cards)
- かるた⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧: karuta tournament
- かるた⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊び：01285_asobi⟧: karuta as a game/pastime

CULTURAL NOTE:
Karuta is traditionally played during New Year's celebrations. In the game, one person reads a clue (the {読|よ}み{札|ふだ} 'reading card') and players compete to be the first to grab the matching {取|と}り{札|ふだ} ('grabbing card'). Competitive karuta based on ⟦{百人一首|ひゃくにんいっしゅ}→百人一首：22329_hyakuninisshu⟧ is recognized as a sport, with top players memorizing all 100 poems and their positions on the playing field.

ETYMOLOGY:
Borrowed from Portuguese 'carta' during the 16th century, when Portuguese missionaries and traders introduced playing cards to Japan.
